# AGENTS.md

Project instructions for AI agents working in this repository. Claude Code
additionally reads [`CLAUDE.md`](CLAUDE.md), which is authoritative for
everything outside the PlanetScale rules below.

**Do not edit this file without the owner's explicit approval.**

## PlanetScale

|                       |                   |
| --------------------- | ----------------- |
| Organization          | `devashishsood18` |
| Database              | `nucarpool`       |
| Engine                | Vitess / MySQL    |
| Production branch     | `main`            |
| Agent-writable branch | `staging`         |
| Other branches        | `test`            |

The CLI may also be authenticated against a personal org (`jo-cho`). Always pass
`--org devashishsood18` explicitly on resource subcommands rather than relying on
the current org.

### Branch policy

- **`main` is production and is READ-ONLY for agents.** Metadata, schema,
  Insights, query errors, schema recommendations, and `SELECT` / `SHOW` /
  `DESCRIBE` / `EXPLAIN` are allowed. Row writes and DDL are forbidden, as is
  creating any production credential.
- **`staging` is the only branch an agent may write.** Writes, schema changes,
  `prisma db push` validation, and backfills or test data are allowed **when
  they are explicitly part of an approved ticket**. Destructive statements still
  require the owner's approval each time.
- **`test` is READ-ONLY** unless the owner explicitly approves otherwise. Note
  that no PlanetScale credential can express "staging but not test" — see
  _Enforcement_ below.

### Safe Migrations

| Branch    | Safe Migrations |
| --------- | --------------- |
| `main`    | **enabled**     |
| `staging` | disabled        |
| `test`    | disabled        |

Safe Migrations on production is server-side enforcement: direct DDL against
`main` is rejected and must go through a deploy request. It does **not** block
row writes — `UPDATE` and `DELETE` are unaffected by it.

### Deploy requests are human-controlled

An agent may **open** a deploy request. An agent may never approve it, ship it,
roll it back, force a cutover, or unblock the queue. The human does that.

`require_approval_for_deploy` on this database was `false` as of 2026-08-27,
which means PlanetScale itself does not require a reviewer; 24 of the first 25
deploy requests reached production with `approved=false`. Until that setting is
turned on, the human gate is convention plus the local guard, not a server-side
control.

### Branch creation

Creating PlanetScale branches is **not** routine agent work here, even though
PlanetScale's own skills treat it as allowed by default. `allow_data_branching`
is enabled, so a branch cut from production can clone real data into a branch
that has no Safe Migrations and many admin credentials. Ask before creating a
branch, and prefer `staging` for schema work.

### Identity expectations

- The agent should authenticate as a **dedicated restricted service token**, not
  a developer's personal OAuth session. A personal session inherits that
  person's full production capability.
- The token must **not** hold `connect_production_branch` (it can mint
  production write credentials) or `approve_deploy_request`.
- Production read queries require `connect_production_read_only_branch` plus
  `delete_production_read_only_branch_password`.
- Never pass a PlanetScale token inline as a command-line flag; use the
  `PLANETSCALE_API_TOKEN` environment variable. An inline token swaps the
  agent's identity and leaks the secret into the transcript.
- MCP: prefer `https://mcp.pscale.dev/mcp/planetscale-insights-only`, which does
  not ship query-execution tools at all. If the full endpoint is used, it must
  be authenticated with the restricted token, never with a full-access OAuth
  grant.

### Enforcement: what is real versus what is written down

Treat this section as the source of truth about how much protection exists.

**Credential-enforced** — holds regardless of what any agent decides to do:

- Safe Migrations on production blocks direct DDL there.
- A token without `connect_production_branch` cannot obtain a production write
  credential.
- A token without `approve_deploy_request` cannot approve a deploy request, and
  PlanetScale separately forbids a token from approving a deploy request that
  the same token created.

**Harness-enforced** — Claude Code only; another agent or a plain shell is
unaffected:

- [`.claude/hooks/pscale-guard.sh`](.claude/hooks/pscale-guard.sh), a
  `PreToolUse` hook, blocks production write roles, deploy-request mutation,
  production credential creation, interactive and proxied production sessions,
  inline tokens, direct MySQL client connections to PlanetScale hosts, and write
  calls to the PlanetScale REST API.
- `permissions.deny` in [`.claude/settings.json`](.claude/settings.json) covers
  the same ground by command prefix, and denies the MCP write-query tool.

**Policy-only** — this file; an instruction, not a control:

- "`test` is read-only." No credential can distinguish `staging` from `test`.
- "Staging writes only on an approved ticket."
- "Production deploy requests are human-controlled", until
  `require_approval_for_deploy` is enabled.
- Everything else in this document.

### Migration files are not applied to PlanetScale

`prisma/migrations/` exists for CI verification only; nothing runs
`prisma migrate deploy` against PlanetScale. Schema promotion is
`prisma db push` to `staging`, then a Deploy Request into production. See
[`src/server/db/README.md`](src/server/db/README.md#changing-the-schema).

### Tooling

- CLI: `pscale`, always with `--format json` in automation. `--org` goes on
  resource subcommands, not on the root command.
- `pscale sql` defaults to the reader role and refuses `DELETE` / `DROP` /
  `TRUNCATE` without `--force`. It does **not** refuse `INSERT`, `UPDATE`, or
  `ALTER` — that gap is what the local guard covers.
- Skills: [planetscale/skills](https://github.com/planetscale/skills) — load
  `14-pscale-cli-automation` for CLI conventions, `00-safe-orchestrator` for a
  full assessment. Autonomous execution mode (skill `13`) is **not** authorized
  on this project.

If any step would broaden access beyond these rules, stop and ask the owner.
